subject: Re: Does it matter if the correlation matrix of latent variables is not positive definite with DWLS factor extraction?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Does it matter if the correlation matrix of latent variables is not positive definite with DWLS factor extraction?
parts:
On 01/04/2016 07:10 AM, Brent Caldwell wrote:
> lavaan WARNING: number of observations (203) too small to compute Gamma

This warning tells you that your sample size (in one group) may be too
small to get a reliable estimate of the 'Gamma' matrix (which is used
for weighting). This may affect the quality of the results. Or not. Hard
to say.

> lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive
> definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

This is more serious. Perhaps you have negative variances? Or highly
correlated factors? In any case, this is a symptom of misfit. Again,
this may be a (small) sample problem.

> of latent variables is not positive definite, given that DWLS does not
> have to rotate the matrix?

Rotate? Rotation has nothing to do with it.

> I tried using ML, but it said that the covariance matrix of
> latent variables was not positive definite in either the smallest ethnic
> group (n=203) nor all the other ethnicities combined (n=1145) which had
> been positive definite with DWLS estimation.

DWLS is often more forgiving, but ML is not. But if both estimators give
you trouble in the smallest group, you may have to conclude that your
sample size (in that group) is just too small, given the size of your model.

> I noticed that if I restricted the analysis to subjects who had complete
> data on all variables

Given that your sample size is already small, I would hesitate to
exclude even more observations.

> hypothesis is that subjects who missed recording one or more of 'age,
> gender, ethnicity, address' were probably rushing their answering of the
> questions and not being attentive and therefore when they completed the
> psychological battery, they probably didn't consider their answers
> carefully, and may have given contradictory answers.

That would be very unfortunate. I am not sure you can repair this.

> However the difftest command has disappeared from R
> in the latest semTools package.

You should use anova() (which calls lavTestLRT) instead. The difftest
function was old and primitive, and certainly did not handle robust test
statistics.

> As far as I can tell, the
> measurementInvariance command assumes data are continuous, not ordinal.
> Is there a way to check for measurement invariance using ordinal data?

See the measurementInvarianceCat() function in semTools.

Yves.
